html:
The Muwekma Ohlone Tribe is a group of descendants of the Ohlone of the San Francisco Bay Area, mostly from the Verona Band of Alameda County. It is the largest of several Ohlone groups, but is not recognized by the United States government.

Their ancestors were the Chochenyo, Tamien and other Ohlone speaking peoples of the East and South Bay, who were brought into Mission San José and other California missions after 1797. After the missions closed, many worked on ranches near Pleasanton and lived in the Verona village. The United States once dealt with the Verona Band, but stopped in the 1920s. The tribe has sought federal acknowledgment since 1989.
